description: Figure 7 illustrates the relationship between the popularity of a subject and the accuracy of a model. The x-axis is labeled “Pop Frequency (x10⁴)” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 19, with tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. There are two lines displayed: a blue solid line with cross markers representing “Initial Accuracy”, and a red solid line with plus markers representing “Final Accuracy”. The “Initial Accuracy” line starts at approximately 0.28 when Pop Frequency is 1, increases to a peak of approximately 0.78 when Pop Frequency is 11, and then declines to approximately 0.62 when Pop Frequency is 19. The “Final Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.34 when Pop Frequency is 1, steadily increases to approximately 0.84 when Pop Frequency is 11, and then declines to approximately 0.68 when Pop Frequency is 19.
